name: Xia Shudong
current_role: Chairman & CEO and controlling shareholder, China TransInfo Technology (千方科技, SZ:002373)
profile: Xia Shudong (b. ~1972, Hubei) founded China TransInfo, a Shenzhen-listed provider of smart-transportation and intelligent-security systems for Chinese cities; Alibaba bought a 15% stake in 2019 for 3.6bn yuan. He still chairs the board and in 2025 launched TranXmart (千曙科技), an autonomous-freight trucking subsidiary.
interesting_fact: In 2025 TransInfo spun up TranXmart (千曙科技), an autonomous-driving freight unit whose stated goal is to build China's largest unmanned freight-capacity platform, using hub-to-hub routes tested in Sichuan/Chongqing and new-energy heavy trucks.
deep_cut_fact: Before business he was an academic mapmaker: after studying at Chongqing University he earned a 2003 PhD in cartography & GIS at Peking University's Institute of Remote Sensing and GIS, and the company began as Beijing PKU ChinaFront (北大千方), a PKU-linked spin-out.
notes: Contact via TransInfo board-secretary office (securities@ctfo.com). Chongqing University detail per WEF profile (page blocks scraping; seen via search).

name: Roy Richardson
current_role: Life President, Richardson family business (Richardsons, West Midlands property)
profile: Roy Richardson (born c.1930) and his late twin Don founded a Black Country business in 1948, moving from used commercial vehicles into property; they turned the derelict Round Oak Steelworks site into the Merry Hill shopping centre in the 1980s. The family business, now run by his sons, invests in property; Roy is Life President.
interesting_fact: The twins bought 400 acres of the closed Round Oak Steelworks (shut 1982, an enterprise zone) and, inspired by US malls, built Merry Hill in eight phases by 1989, one of Europe's largest shopping centres.
deep_cut_fact: He and Don left school at 14 to work for their father selling used commercial vehicles, often post-war surplus, and did RAF national service together before starting in business in 1948. He was the first businessman made an Honorary Freeman of Sandwell (2018).
notes: Now in his 90s; day-to-day business is run by sons (Lee, Carl, Martyn). Twin Don died 2007. Sandwell freedom: https://www.expressandstar.com/business/standing-ovation-as-dr-roy-richardson-made-honorary-freeman-of-sandwell-with-video-6241724 ; alive status inferred from no death reports and 2025 Rich List coverage naming him head of family.

name: Li Xinyu
current_role: Founder, Chairman and controlling shareholder, Talkweb Information System (拓维信息, SZ:002261); also chairs Kaihong Zhigu (开鸿智谷)
profile: Li Xinyu founded Changsha-based Talkweb in 1996; it listed in Shenzhen in 2008 and grew from mobile value-added and education services into a full-stack Huawei-ecosystem partner (Kunpeng/Ascend servers, AI computing, OpenHarmony OS). He remains chairman and holds ~11.7% of the company.
interesting_fact: Talkweb is a core partner in Huawei's Ascend AI-compute ecosystem and participates in China's 'East Data, West Computing' data-center program, offering chips-to-servers-to-OS-to-apps solutions; in 2026 Li gave a keynote at the OpenAtom open-source ecosystem conference.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Talkweb he worked at the Hunan Provincial Electric Power Bureau, giving up that 'iron rice bowl' state job in 1996 to start the company in Changsha.
notes: Energy/data-center relevant (former power-bureau employee; AI compute and 'East Data West Computing'). Power-bureau detail is from a single eastmoney caifuhao article; not cross-checked elsewhere.

name: Wong Tsu-Hing
current_role: Executive Director & Group General Manager, Dah Sing Financial Holdings (HK:0440); Vice Chairman, MD & Chief Executive, Dah Sing Bank
profile: Harold Tsu-Hing Wong (王祖興, ~56) is the son of chairman David Shou-Yeh Wong, whose family controls Hong Kong's Dah Sing banking group (founded 1947). He joined Dah Sing Bank in 2000, ran Dah Sing Banking Group as CEO 2011-2017 and now heads Dah Sing Bank and is group general manager of the listed holding company.
interesting_fact: Dah Sing is often described as one of the last independent, family-controlled local banks in Hong Kong; the Wong family wealth is listed jointly for Harold and his father David (b. ~1941), who still chairs the group.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a lawyer before banking: LLB (Hons) from King's College London and a Harvard MBA, and is a qualified solicitor in both England & Wales and Hong Kong; he sits on the Executive Committee of the Hong Kong Institute of Bankers.
notes: Hurun lists fortune shared with father Wong Shou-Yeh (David Wong). No published IR/press email found; route via Dah Sing Bank corporate communications / company secretary (Richard Tsung-Yung Li).

name: Liu Jianwei
current_role: Chairman, President and controlling shareholder, Shenzhen H&T Intelligent Control (和而泰, SZ:002402)
profile: Liu Jianwei (b. 1964) is a former Harbin Institute of Technology professor and automatic-control specialist who founded Shenzhen H&T in 2000; it makes intelligent controllers for home appliances, power tools, autos and smart products, with plants in China, Europe and North America. He holds ~13% and remains chairman and president.
interesting_fact: H&T began as a university spin-out: its predecessor, Shenzhen H&T Electronic Technology, was set up on 12 Jan 2000 with HIT's industrial development company among the original shareholders, and Liu as legal representative.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an entrepreneur he was a professor at Harbin Institute of Technology's School of Astronautics and later at HIT's Shenzhen Graduate School.
notes: Board secretary listed in filings as Luo Shanshan. Low media profile.

name: Gao Yuanqian
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Director, COO and CTO, Shenzhen Edge Medical (精锋医疗, HK:2675)
profile: Gao Yuanqian, a Tianjin University mechanical-engineering PhD, co-founded Shenzhen-based surgical-robot maker Edge Medical in May 2017 with her husband Wang Jianchen. Its MP1000 multi-port and SP1000 single-port laparoscopic robots are approved in China and CE-marked; the company listed in Hong Kong on 8 Jan 2026, with the couple holding ~49% pre-IPO.
interesting_fact: Edge Medical was registered on 4 May 2017 with just 100,000 yuan of capital; by its last pre-IPO round in Oct 2021 it was valued at about US$1.5bn, more than 230x its angel valuation. Shares rose 30%+ on IPO day in Jan 2026.
deep_cut_fact: Her PhD was a joint program between Tianjin University and the Surgical Navigation and Robotics Lab at Harvard Medical School (PhD awarded June 2017, a month after she co-founded Edge); her husband/co-founder did his joint program at MIT.
notes: Fortune shared with husband/co-founder Wang Jianchen (CEO). Contact form includes a 'media inquiry' category. Young (post-'85) founder; Hurun Global U40 2026.

name: The Warburton family
current_role: Owners of Warburtons, the UK's largest bakery; Jonathan Warburton is Chairman, cousins Brett and Ross Warburton are fifth-generation directors
profile: The Warburton family has owned Bolton-based Warburtons since Thomas and Ellen Warburton began baking in 1876. The fifth generation (Jonathan, Ross and Brett) took control in 1991 and turned a northern regional baker into a national brand with ~5,000 staff producing over 2 million bakery products a day.
interesting_fact: In 1876, during a grocery slump, Ellen Warburton baked her first batch of four loaves and six cakes in the family's Bolton grocery shop; they sold out within an hour and within two weeks the shop was renamed 'Warburtons the Bakers'.
deep_cut_fact: Chairman Jonathan Warburton started his career at Unilever before joining the family firm at 23, received an honorary doctorate from Manchester University in 2003, and describes himself as skiing 'enthusiastically' and playing golf 'erratically'. Brett Warburton chaired food-research body Campden BRI 2011-16.
notes: Family entry; Jonathan Warburton (chairman) is the public face and appears in TV ads. Best route: Warburtons Press Office, Bolton.

name: Yu Xin
current_role: Chairwoman and co-controlling shareholder (with Li Aiwu), Hunan Zhongke Electric (中科电气, SZ:300035)
profile: Yu Xin (b. June 1967), a woman entrepreneur from Yueyang, Hunan, has chaired Hunan Zhongke Electric since 2008. The company began in electromagnetic steelmaking equipment (continuous-casting EMS, lifting magnets) and has pivoted into graphite anode materials for lithium-ion batteries, now its core business.
interesting_fact: Zhongke Electric is a play on both steel and EV/energy storage: alongside magnetic equipment for steel mills it is a major supplier of graphite anode materials for lithium batteries.
deep_cut_fact: She started her career in 1989 at the Yueyang Lifting Electromagnet Factory, worked there nearly a decade, then served as finance director before becoming chair of Yueyang Zhongke Electromagnetic Technology, the predecessor business.
notes: Fortune shared with co-controller Li Aiwu. Board secretary: Lu Yan. Strong energy-storage angle for the podcast. Researched from exchange-data pages only (web search budget exhausted).

name: Yin Xingman
current_role: Actual controller (~12.9%) of Xinzhi Group (信质集团, SZ:002664); son Yin Wei is chairman
profile: Yin Xingman built Xinzhi from a small township collective in Jiaojiang, Taizhou (Zhejiang) making auto generators into a listed maker of motor cores and stator/rotor assemblies for new-energy vehicle drive motors, compressors, elevators and appliances. He remains actual controller; his son Yin Wei (McGill graduate, b. 1981) chairs the company.
interesting_fact: Xinzhi supplies drive-motor stator and rotor cores and hairpin stator assemblies for new-energy vehicles, plus fuel-cell vehicle motors and hub-motor stators.
deep_cut_fact: The company's roots are a township collective with just 210,000 yuan of registered capital, with Yin Xingman as legal representative, making automobile generators and solenoid valves (with electrical repair as a sideline) on Jiaobei Street; it was renamed Taizhou Auto Motor Factory in 1995.
notes: No current executive title found for Yin Xingman; day-to-day led by son Yin Wei (chairman). No news check on health/alive status possible (search budget exhausted). Board secretary: Chen Shihai.

name: Wang Zhong
current_role: Second-largest shareholder (~20.1%) of Jiangshan Oupai Door Industry (江山欧派, SH:603208); no current board/executive role listed
profile: Wang Zhong is co-founder and long-time No. 2 shareholder of Jiangshan Oupai, a Zhejiang maker of molded, engineered-wood doors and cabinetry. With Wu Shuigen he ran the Jiangshan Oupai Decorative Materials Factory from 2004-06 before Wu founded Jiangshan Oupai Door in 2006; the company listed in Shanghai in 2017.
interesting_fact: As of 30 Sep 2026 he still held about 20.1% of Jiangshan Oupai, second only to chairman Wu Shuigen (29.4%).
deep_cut_fact: The business started as the Jiangshan Oupai Decorative Materials Factory (江山市欧派装饰材料厂), which he ran with Wu Shuigen from 2004 to 2006 in Jiangshan, Quzhou, before it became a door company.
notes: Very low profile; not on the board or management team. Name is common, but the Oupai shareholding confirms the person. Only route is via company securities office (board secretary Chen Chunjin). Search budget exhausted, so limited research.

name: Kang Ning
current_role: Co-founder of Beijing Jetsen Technology (捷成股份, SZ:300182); no current board/management role found
profile: Kang Ning co-founded Beijing Jetsen in August 2006 with Xu Ziquan, Xu Ting and Zheng Qiang; it listed on ChiNext in 2011. Jetsen began in audio-video systems for broadcasters and moved into film/TV production and distribution, new-media copyright operations and digital marketing.
